summary: No blocking QA findings in the inspected workspace. The shipped app matches the round-3 scope I could verify directly: 6 compact candidate previews, Korean-first score-hidden UI, editable role preferences, localStorage-backed saved-player save/load with exact-10 gating, candidate selection, and immediate two-click swap editing with refreshed tier/preference metadata.
strengths: `npm test` and `npm run build` both pass on the current workspace state, and the output remains a static frontend bundle under `dist/`.

Direct source inspection plus targeted runtime checks confirm the canonical `matchPlayers` flow, saved-preference hydration for pasted names, exact-10 saved-player loading, and textarea rewrite with canonical header TSV.

`src/lib/optimizer.js` and runtime verification confirm 6 visible candidates, valid `1탱 2딜 2힐` composition per team, no duplicate player assignment within a candidate, and ranking keyed by total score difference, role-score-difference sum, tank difference, then unranked difference.

`src/lib/editor.js`, `src/lib/render.js`, and the app-flow checks confirm that candidate selection loads a fresh editor, two slot clicks swap players immediately, and destination-slot tier plus preference-rank data recalculate after the swap while numeric score surfaces stay hidden.
`README.md` and `FINAL_OUTPUT.md` are aligned with the shipped behavior and accurately disclose the remaining optional browser-smoke gap in this sandbox.
verification_run: `npm run test:browser` (fails here because no Chromium-family browser binary is installed in the sandbox; current spec marks this gap non-blocking)
`rg -n "Final Edit|compact preview|TANK|DPS|SUP|scoreDifference|팀 A 총점|팀 B 총점|점수 차이|역할군 차이 합|탱커 차이|언랭 분배 차이" src dist README.md FINAL_OUTPUT.md`

Targeted `node --input-type=module` checks against `src/lib/appFlow.js`, `src/lib/playerStore.js`, `src/lib/optimizer.js`, `src/lib/editor.js`, and `src/lib/render.js` to verify header/headerless parsing, saved-player hydration, 6-candidate rendering, hidden-score UI, candidate reselection reset, and swap recalculation
release_readiness: Release-ready for this iteration. Residual risk remains around optional real-browser smoke execution because Chromium is unavailable in this sandbox, but that gap is explicitly documented and is non-blocking under the current spec.
